title: Encrypted MemoryStore SQLite database at rest
problem: MemoryStore kept durable agent memories and TODO plans in a plaintext SQLite database at ~/Library/Application Support/Trinity S3AI/AgentMemory/agent-memory.sqlite3. Any process with user access could read every memory body and plan goal, including recalled snippets that might contain sensitive context.
root_cause: MemoryStore opened and closed a plaintext SQLite file directly. There was no encryption boundary around the database on disk, and the WAL journal mode created additional plaintext -wal/-shm files.
fix: Added TriOSEncryption(keyName: "memory") shared named key. Created EncryptedMemoryStore helper that manages an AES-256-GCM encrypted snapshot (agent-memory.sqlite3.enc). Updated MemoryStore to decrypt the snapshot into a temporary working file on open, run SQLite with journal_mode=DELETE/synchronous=FULL, and re-encrypt + securely delete the working file on close. Added automatic migration from a legacy plaintext agent-memory.sqlite3. Bumped schema version to 2. Fixed MemoryStoreFTSTests broken PersistentMemoryStore reference and added MemoryStoreEncryptionTests covering ciphertext indistinguishability, round-trip recall, and legacy migration.

tests.build_sh: PASS (chat integration tests PASS; swift test auto-skipped because XCTest is unavailable in this toolchain)
tests.swift_test: SKIPPED (XCTest not available in CommandLineTools-only environment)

variants.A: File-level encrypted snapshot — encrypt/decrypt the whole SQLite file on close/open. Self-contained, no new dependencies, but working copy is plaintext while store is open. — implemented
variants.B: SQLCipher native SQLite encryption — strongest at-rest story and WAL-compatible, but requires building/linking libsqlcipher and conflicts with the current swiftc -lsqlite3 direct build path.
variants.C: Per-conversation encrypted memory shards — split memory/plan tables into separate encrypted SQLite files per conversationId for blast-radius control; adds multi-database fan-out complexity.

lessons: File-level encryption is landable immediately when native SQLite encryption is blocked by the build environment; the resting state is protected and legacy databases migrate transparently.
WAL mode is incompatible with file-level snapshots because -wal/-shm files leak plaintext outside the encrypted snapshot; switch to DELETE journal mode with synchronous=FULL.
Schema migration for an unchanged table layout can be just a user_version bump, keeping migrations trivial while still versioning the encrypted-store era.
Securely deleting the transient working file (overwrite + unlink) is best-effort; the real long-term fix is native page encryption (SQLCipher) so there is no plaintext working copy.
A small helper enum (EncryptedMemoryStore) isolates file-system and CryptoKit details from the actor, preserving the existing AgentMemoryStoreProtocol contract.
